:::{#thm-eigen-triangular}
#### The eigenvalues of an upper triangular matrix are its diagonal entries

The eigenvalues (@def-eigenvalue) of an upper triangular $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{U}$
(@def-triangular-matrix) are exactly its diagonal entries $u_{11}, \ldots, u_{pp}$.

:::

::: proof

$\matr{U} - \eigval\,\matr{I}_p$ is upper triangular,
with diagonal entries $u_{ii} - \eigval$ (@def-identity-matrix, @def-matrix-addition).

**If $\eigval$ is not a diagonal entry,**
every $u_{ii} - \eigval \ne 0$, so $(\matr{U} - \eigval\,\matr{I}_p)\,\vecf{v} = \vzero$
has exactly one solution, $\vecf{v} = \vzero$ (@thm-back-substitution),
and $\eigval$ is not an eigenvalue (@thm-eigenvalue-singular).

**If $\eigval$ is a diagonal entry,**
let $k$ be the smallest index with $u_{kk} = \eigval$,
and write $\matr{M} = \matr{U} - \eigval\,\matr{I}_p$, so $m_{kk} = 0$ and $m_{ii} \ne 0$ for $i < k$.
Look for $\vecf{v}$ with $v_k = 1$ and $v_j = 0$ for $j > k$.
Entry $i$ of $\matr{M} \vecf{v}$ is

$$
\ba
\sumjp m_{ij}\,v_j
&= \sum_{j=i}^{p} m_{ij}\,v_j
&& \text{(} m_{ij} = 0 \text{ for } j < i \text{)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=i}^{k} m_{ij}\,v_j,
&& \text{(} v_j = 0 \text{ for } j > k \text{)}
\ea
$$

where the last sum is empty, and so $0$, when $i > k$. So:

- for $i > k$ entry $i$ is $0$;
- for $i = k$ it is $m_{kk}\,v_k = 0$;
- for $i < k$ it is $0$ exactly when
  $v_i = -\frac{1}{m_{ii}} \sum_{j=i+1}^{k} m_{ij}\,v_j$,
  and these equations fix $v_{k-1}, \ldots, v_1$ in turn, as in @thm-back-substitution.

So $\matr{M} \vecf{v} = \vzero$ with $v_k = 1$, hence $\vecf{v} \ne \vzero$,
and $\eigval$ is an eigenvalue.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-eigen-triangular}
#### Eigenvalues read off the diagonal

$\matr{U} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$
of @exm-triangular-matrix has eigenvalues $2$, $\tfrac{1}{2}$ and $-1$.
For $\eigval = \tfrac{1}{2}$ (so $k = 2$), take $v_2 = 1$, $v_3 = 0$;
row 1 of $(\matr{U} - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{I}_3)\,\vecf{v}$ is $\tfrac{3}{2}\,v_1 + 1 = 0$, so $v_1 = -\tfrac{2}{3}$.
Check:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{U}\,(-\tfrac{2}{3}, 1, 0) &= (-\tfrac{4}{3} + 1, \tfrac{1}{2}, 0) \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,(-\tfrac{2}{3}, 1, 0).
\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix $\matr{J}$ of @exm-eigenspace is upper triangular with both diagonal entries $0$,
and $0$ is its only eigenvalue.

:::
